transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Tomás Ortega (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Cobalt Head of AI), Ben Chu (Cobalt Dir Platform), Lena Park (Cobalt Sec & Compliance)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in; primary themes: committed capacity uplift vs burst add-on economics, adding EU region for data residency, timeline for contract extension, and security questions around KMS/SSO and audit logs. Agreed to run a short dedicated benchmark and exchange security artifacts.

Topics:
- Current usage pattern and forecast
- Dedicated pool sizing and burst pricing
- Private/VPC onprem constraints and EU residency
- Security artifacts (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
- Next steps and schedule for benchmark

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey thanks everyone for joining, um we wanted to kick off with a quick agenda, renewal timing, capacity uplift, and then the EU / private residency ask. quick check, is that good?
[00:12] Aisha: yeah that works for us, thanks Maya. just to flag, we've got a board review window mid-march so we're hoping to have numbers and a recommended path before then.
[00:23] Ben: hi all, Ben here - i'll speak to platform constraints. currently we're at about 120 qps peak for inference and month is roughly 1.2B tokens, ah roughly, uh monthly.
[00:36] Tomás: ok got it, and that's across hosted today?
[00:40] Ben: correct, we've been on hosted with Redwood for last 10 months, no private yet.
[00:46] Maya: and the ask from the renew side is twofold, one is a committed uplift - they're looking at a 2x reserved capacity for steady state - and second is the ability to burst to a higher tier during peak retail moments. so we're proposing Dedicated + burst add-on.
[01:03] Lena: from a compliance perspective we also need EU region activation and, um, data residency guarantees for any EU traffic. plus KMS integration detail, and audit log retention.
[01:15] Aisha: yeah can't understate the residency piece, European regulatory teams are strict, so we need both logical isolation and logs.
[01:23] Maya: totally makes sense. tomas, can you talk through how Dedicated vs Private would look for them? and the fallback behavior if capacity saturates?
[01:33] Tomás: sure. so Dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool in our managed infra - predictable throughput and you can pin model versions. Private (VPC) is the path if you need customer-managed network and deeper isolation. quick note, in Dedicated we support prefix/KV cache and automatic batching, which helps token economics. if the pool saturates we have smart routing to fallback to hosted variants that are compatible - slight latency bump but keeps you online.
[02:02] Ben: how noticeable is that latency bump? our SLAs aim for p95 under 850ms, we're currently averaging ~420ms.
[02:11] Tomás: it depends on model size and kv hit rate; typical bump is 150-400ms at p95 on fallback, so can exceed your 850ms target in worst-case. but we can architect a hybrid: keep a small dedicated reserve for critical routes and route non-critical paths to hosted.
[02:31] Aisha: ok so we likely need a two-tier plan. keep critical scoring/credit decisions on dedicated, put user-facing chat on hosted fallback.
[02:40] Maya: that aligns with the cost conversation. dedicated unit economics are better for steady state, burst is priced as an add-on. i'll send a worked example.
[02:49] Speaker 2: (crosstalk)
[02:52] Lena: security, two specific asks: KMS integration with our cloud provider (we use AZ KMS), and proof of key access separation. also, do you retain raw prompts in any systems?
[03:06] Tomás: for KMS we support envelope encryption and can integrate with AWS/Azure KMS via customer keys - for Redwood Private we'd surface customer-managed keys. we do have audit logs but retention windows vary by plan - i'll include exact retention tables in the pack. as for prompts, by default hosted logs minimal telemetry for debugging, but we can disable retention or enable token redaction.
[03:29] Ben: what's the onboarding lead time for EU region activation if we go Dedicated?
[03:34] Maya: typical lead time for EU dedicated pool is 3-5 weeks assuming no infra constraints. for Private onprem it's multi-week plus infra provisioning, usually 6-10 weeks.
[03:47] Aisha: hmm board wants fast path — would a short pilot dedicated pool for 2 weeks be possible to show numbers?
[03:55] Tomás: yes, we can spin a small dedicated pilot (2-4 GPUs) and run your benchmark trace; it's typically a 1-week setup and then benchmark runs. cost is prorated and counted towards future commitment if you convert.
[04:12] Maya: perfect. let's talk economics — Ben, you mentioned 2x committed steady state. do you have a ballpark of the commitment term? 6 months, annual?
[04:23] Ben: board preference is 6 months to match product roadmap; they don't want multi-year right now.
[04:29] Maya: ok we'll model a 6-month commitment with burst add-on and include a mid-term review clause.
[04:36] Aisha: also curious about quantization options — are there verified quantized variants that reduce cost without hurting our scoring fidelity?
[04:43] Tomás: yes we have quantized builds for many open models — Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization level by workload; for scoring tasks we'd test for regression. we'll put recommended profiles in the benchmark writeup.
[04:58] Lena: another security question: SSO/SAML support and RBAC for token-level access? and where do audit events go?
[05:06] Maya: we support SAML SSO and RBAC in the Console; audit events can forward to customer SIEM via syslog or delivered as a daily export for private deployments.
[05:19] Ben: network constraints — we have strict egress caps at our colo, need to know approx egress for EU activation and if there's a local edge option.
[05:28] Tomás: we'll calculate egress estimates based on your qps and avg token sizes — that'll be in the benchmark sheet. we do have EU edge nodes which reduce cross-region egress if traffic stays local.
[05:41] Speaker 1: (laughs)
[05:43] Maya: ok next, timeline and milestones: board deck early-mid March, benchmark week w/c 7th March, contract amendment by 10th March? Thoughts?
[05:54] Aisha: that timeline is tight but doable if Cobalt ops gets data to you by end of this week.
[06:01] Ben: we can probably extract logs and the token profile by friday.
[06:06] Lena: security needs to run a quick gap analysis on SOC2 scope — can you include an extract of evidentiary controls?
[06:14] Tomás: yes i'll include SOC2 cert summary and a controller vs processor writeup; also a short doc on how KMS flows work with dedicated and private.
[06:26] Maya: great. any objections on the approach?
[06:29] Aisha: none from product; main risk is latency during extreme bursts but the hybrid plan mitigates that.
[06:36] Ben: cost is the other risk, but if we see the benchmark and a model of quantization gains that could justify the 6-month commit.
[06:46] Maya: ok we'll send a worked example with three scenarios: conservative (1.5x commit), aggressive (2x commit + quant), and pilot-first (small dedicated + burst) — that'll include estimated monthly spend, p95 latency, and SLA implications.
[06:59] Speaker 3: (phone beep)
[07:01] Lena: one more Q: for audit logs, can retention be extended to 13 months on request?
[07:07] Tomás: on dedicated/private yes — we can extend retention with a paid add-on. hosted default is 90 days.
[07:15] Maya: noted. Ok to recap next steps?
[07:18] Aisha: yes please.
[07:20] Maya: Redwood to deliver: pricing workbook and burst sheet, SOC2 & KMS notes, benchmark runbook. Cobalt to deliver: token profile, qps, and egress constraints. schedule benchmark for week of 7th.
[07:34] Ben: I'll get the token CSV and fetch the sample traffic by friday.
[07:39] Aisha: i'll prepare a one-pager for the board with the three scenarios once we have the cost numbers.
[07:45] Maya: perfect, i'll follow up with calendar invites and the benchmark template. thanks all.
[07:50] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality and idiosyncrasies:
